title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.en: Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
units.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
units.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess. The crown prince also hoped that marrying into the Han family would strengthen his position.

units.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
units.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
units.idiomatic: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

units.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
units.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

units.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
units.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
units.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

units.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
units.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
units.idiomatic: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

units.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
units.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.
units.idiomatic: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

units.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
units.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
units.idiomatic: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

title.zh: 卷二十三 列傳第四 褚淵 淵弟澄 徐嗣 王儉
title.en: Volume 23 Biographies 4: Chu Yuan, Yuan Dicheng, Xu Si, Wang Jian
title.raw: 卷二十三 列傳第四 褚淵 淵弟澄 徐嗣 王儉 Volume 23 Biographies 4: Chu Yuan, Yuan Dicheng, Xu Si, Wang Jian

units.zh: 南齊書卷二十三‧列傳第四
units.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4
units.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4

units.zh: 褚淵字彥回，河南陽翟人也。
units.literal: Chu Yuan, styled Yanhui, was a native of Yangdi in Henan.
units.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, styled Yanhui, was a man of Yangdi in Henan.

units.zh: 祖秀之，宋太常。
units.literal: His grandfather Xiuzhi was Grand Master of Ceremonies under Song.
units.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuzhi had been Grand Master of Ceremonies under the Song.

units.zh: 上相星連有變，淵憂之，表遜位。
units.literal: The Superior Minister star showed linked changes; Yuan was troubled and memorialized to yield his post.
units.idiomatic: The Superior Minister star showed linked disturbances; troubled, Yuan memorialized to yield his post.

units.zh: 又因王儉及侍中王晏口陳於世祖，世祖不許。
units.literal: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan speak orally before Shizu; Shizu did not consent.
units.idiomatic: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan plead in person before Shizu; Shizu refused.

units.zh: 又啓曰：「臣顧惟凡薄，福過災生，未能以正情自安，遠慚彥輔。
units.literal: He memorialized again, saying, "Your servant reflects on his common mediocrity—blessing has outrun merit and calamity is born; unable to settle his heart in rectitude, far ashamed before worthy counselors.
units.idiomatic: He wrote again: "Your servant knows himself common and slight—favor has outstripped desert and trouble follows; I cannot quiet my heart in truth and am ashamed before worthy counselors.

units.zh: 乃改授司空，領驃騎將軍，侍中、錄尚書如故。
units.literal: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, with Supernal General, Palace Attendant and Recorder unchanged.
units.idiomatic: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, retaining Supernal General, Palace Attendant, and Recorder as before.

units.zh: 上遣侍中王晏黃門郎王秀之問疾。
units.literal: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to inquire after his illness.
units.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to ask after his health.

units.zh: 薨，家無餘財，負債至數十萬。
units.literal: He died; the household had no surplus wealth, debts running to hundreds of thousands.
units.idiomatic: He died; the family left no surplus, and debts ran into the hundreds of thousands.

units.zh: 其年疾，上親臨視，薨，年三十八。
units.literal: That year he fell ill; the emperor personally visited him. He died, aged thirty-eight.
units.idiomatic: That year he sickened; the emperor came in person to his bedside. He died at thirty-eight.

units.zh: 吏部尚書王晏啓及儉喪，上答曰：「儉年德富盛，志用方隆，豈意暴疾，不展救護，便爲異世，奄忽如此，痛酷彌深。
units.literal: Wang Yan, Minister of the Masters of Personnel, memorialized on Jian's death. The emperor replied, "Jian's years and virtue were in fullest flower, his ambition and use just rising—who could have thought a sudden illness, with no scope for healing, would place him in another world so abruptly? The pain is unbearably deep.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel, wrote on Jian's death. The emperor answered: "Jian's years and virtue stood at their height, his will and work just ascending—who could have thought a sudden sickness, with no room for cure, would cast him so quickly into another world? The pain cuts unbearably deep.

units.zh: 其契闊艱運，義重常懷，言尋悲切，不能自勝。
units.literal: His trials through hard fates, his constant weight of right feeling—to speak of them is grief that cuts; I cannot master myself.
units.idiomatic: His shared trials through hard times, the weight of right feeling I always bore—to speak of it is grief I cannot hold in.

title.zh: 卷一百十四 周書5: 世宗本紀一
title.en: Volume 114 Book of Later Zhou 16: Shizong Annals 1
title.raw: 卷一百十四 周書5: 世宗本紀一 Volume 114 Book of Later Zhou 16: Shizong Annals 1

units.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，諱榮，太祖之養子，蓋聖穆皇后之侄也。
units.literal: The Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Ruiwu Xiaowen, whose personal name was Rong, was the adopted son of Taizu and was in fact a nephew of Empress Shengmu.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, posthumously known as Ruiwu Xiaowen, bore the personal name Rong. He was Taizu's adopted son and a nephew of Empress Shengmu.

units.zh: 本姓柴氏，父守禮，太子少保致仕。
units.literal: His original surname was the Chai clan; his father was Shouli, who had retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
units.idiomatic: He was born into the Chai family. His father Shouli had retired from the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：柴翁者，嘗獨居室，人以為司冥事。
units.literal: (The Longpingji states: There was an Old Man Chai who once lived alone in his room, and people thought he dealt with matters of the underworld.
units.idiomatic: (According to the Longpingji, an elder of the Chai clan once lived alone in his room, and people believed he had dealings with the realm of the dead.

units.zh: 庚辰，幸南莊。
units.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor visited the South Manor.
units.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor visited the South Manor.

units.zh: 辛巳，荊南節度使、南平王高保融加守中書令，夏州節度使、西平王李彜興加守太保，西京留守武行德、徐州王晏、鄧州侯章並加兼中書令。
units.literal: On xinsi, Gao Baorong, military governor of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping, was advanced to Defender Councilor; Li Yixing, military governor of Xiazhou and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, Wang Yan of Xuzhou, and Hou Zhang of Dengzhou were all additionally made Councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
units.idiomatic: On xinsi Jingnan military governor and Prince of Nanping Gao Baorong was advanced to Defender Councilor; Xiazhou military governor and Prince of Xiping Li Yixing was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde, Xuzhou's Wang Yan, and Dengzhou's Hou Zhang were all additionally made councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 癸未，湖南王進逵加兼中書令；
units.literal: On guimao, Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
units.idiomatic: On guimao Hunan's Wang Jinkui was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

units.zh: 冬十月甲辰，左羽林大將軍孟漢卿賜死，坐監納厚取耗餘也。
units.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Meng Hanqing, Major General of the Left Feathered Forest, was granted death for supervising collection and taking a heavy surplus in collection.
units.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiachen Left Feathered Forest Major General Meng Hanqing was ordered to take his own life for skimming excess grain while supervising tax collection.

units.zh: 丙午，以安州節度使李洪義為青州節度使，以貝州節度使王饒為相州節度使，以徐州節度使王晏為西京留守，以西京留守武行德為徐州節度使。
units.literal: On bingwu, Li Hongyi, military governor of Anzhou, was made military governor of Qingzhou; Wang Rao, military governor of Beizhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Wang Yan, military governor of Xuzhou, was made Western Capital resident defender; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, was made military governor of Xuzhou.
units.idiomatic: On bingwu Anzhou military governor Li Hongyi was moved to Qingzhou; Beizhou military governor Wang Rao to Xiangzhou; Xuzhou military governor Wang Yan to Western Capital defender; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde to Xuzhou military governor.

units.zh: 戊申，以龍捷左廂都指揮使、泗州防禦使韓令坤為洋州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使；
units.literal: On wushen, Han Lingkun, commander of the Dragon Swift Left Wing and defense commissioner of Sizhou, was made military governor of Yangzhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;
units.idiomatic: On wushen Dragon Swift Left Wing commander and Sizhou defense commissioner Han Lingkun was made Yangzhou military governor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;

title.zh: 卷三十二 本紀第三十二 高宗九
title.en: Volume 32 Annals 32: Gaozong 9
title.raw: 卷三十二 本紀第三十二 高宗九 Volume 32 Annals 32: Gaozong 9

units.zh: 三十一年春正月甲戌朔，以日食，不受朝。
units.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, day jiaxu new moon: because of a solar eclipse, court audience was not held.
units.idiomatic: Year 31, spring, jiaxu new moon: Gaozong canceled audience for the eclipse.

units.zh: 丁丑，雷。
units.literal: Day dingchou: thunder.
units.idiomatic: On dingchou, thunder rolled.

units.zh: 丁亥，免湖州增丁所輸絹。
units.literal: Day dinghai: the silk paid by Huzhou for added registered households was remitted.
units.idiomatic: On dinghai, Huzhou was freed from added-household silk levies.

units.zh: 乙未，行新造會子於淮、浙、湖北、京西諸州。
units.literal: Day yiwei: newly minted exchange notes were put into circulation in the Huai, Zhe, Hubei, and Jingxi prefectures.
units.idiomatic: On yiwei, new exchange notes circulated in the Huai, Zhe, Hubei, and Jingxi.

units.zh: 是月，金主亮徙都汴京，命其臣劉萼由唐、鄧瞰荊、襄，張中彥、王彥章據秦、鳳、窺巴、蜀，蘇保衡、完顏鄭家奴由海道趨兩浙。
units.literal: That month, the Jin ruler Hailing moved the capital to Bianjing; he ordered his minister Liu E from Tang and Deng to overlook Jing and Xiang; Zhang Zhongyan and Wang Yanchang to hold Qin and Feng and spy on Ba and Shu; Su Baoheng and Wanyan Zhengjianu by sea toward the two Zhes.
units.idiomatic: That month Hailing moved to Bianjing; Liu E threatened Jing and Xiang from Tang and Deng; Zhang Zhongyan and Wang Yanchang menaced Ba and Shu from Qin and Feng; Su Baoheng and Wanyan Zhengjianu sailed toward Zhe.

units.zh: 八月辛丑朔，忠義人魏勝復海州，李寶承制以勝知州事。
units.literal: Eighth month, day xinchou new moon: loyalist Wei Sheng recovered Haizhou; Li Bao, by provisional order, made Sheng prefect.
units.idiomatic: Eighth month, xinchou new moon: Wei Sheng retook Haizhou; Li Bao made him prefect.

units.zh: 丙辰，金主亮入廬州，王權自昭關遁，金人追至尉子橋，破敵軍統制姚興戰死，權退保和州。
units.literal: Day bingchen: the Jin ruler Hailing entered Luzhou; Wang Quan fled from Zhaoguan; the Jin pursued to Weizi Bridge; Break-the-Enemy controller Yao Xing died fighting; Quan fell back to defend Hezhou.
units.idiomatic: On bingchen, Hailing entered Luzhou; Wang Quan fled Zhaoguan; at Weizi Bridge Yao Xing fell; Quan held Hezhou.

units.zh: 金州都統制王彥遣統制任天錫出洵陽，復豐陽縣。
units.literal: Jinzhou overall commander Wang Yan sent controller Ren Tiansi out of Xunyang and recovered Fengyang county.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan's Ren Tiansi left Xunyang and retook Fengyang.

units.zh: 丁巳，帝聞王權敗，召楊存中同宰執議於內殿，陳康伯贊帝定議親征。
units.literal: Day dingsi: the Emperor, hearing Wang Quan was defeated, summoned Yang Cunzhong with the chief ministers to discuss in the inner hall; Chen Kangbo praised the Emperor for fixing on campaigning in person.
units.idiomatic: On dingsi, hearing of Wang Quan's defeat, Gaozong called Yang Cunzhong and the councilors within; Chen Kangbo praised his resolve to take the field.

units.zh: 金主亮焚其舟而去。
units.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing burned his boats and left.
units.idiomatic: Hailing burned his boats and withdrew.

units.zh: 戊寅，王彥遣將楊堅復欒川縣。
units.literal: Day wuyin: Wang Yan sent General Yang Jian to recover Luanchuan county.
units.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Yan's Yang Jian retook Luanchuan.

units.zh: 己卯，以湯思退為行宮留守。
units.literal: Day jimao: Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.
units.idiomatic: On jimao, Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.

units.zh: 復犯襄陽，統制官李勝等拒卻之，復通化軍。
units.literal: They again attacked Xiangyang; controller Li Sheng and others repelled them and restored Tonghua army.
units.idiomatic: They struck Xiangyang again; controller Li Sheng and others drove them off and restored Tonghua army.

units.zh: 王彥遣將楊堅、黨清至西京長水縣及金人戰，敗之。
units.literal: Wang Yan sent generals Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui county west of the Western Capital and fought the Jin, defeating them.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui west of the Western Capital, fought the Jin, and won.

units.zh: 庚寅，復長水縣。
units.literal: Day gengyin: Changshui county was restored.
units.idiomatic: On gengyin, Changshui county was restored.

units.zh: 十二月己亥朔，趙撙夜襲蔡州，復入其城。
units.literal: Twelfth month, day jihai new moon: Zhao Zong by night raided Cai prefecture and re-entered its walls.
units.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jihai new moon: Zhao Zong night-raided Cai prefecture and re-entered the city.

units.zh: 王彥遣兵復福昌縣。
units.literal: Wang Yan sent troops to recover Fuchang county.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent troops to retake Fuchang county.

units.zh: 庚子，楊存中及虞允文渡江至瓜州察金兵。
units.literal: Day gengzi: Yang Cunzhong and Yu Yunwen crossed the river to Guazhou to inspect Jin troops.
units.idiomatic: On gengzi, Yang Cunzhong and Yu Yunwen crossed to Guazhou to scout the Jin.

units.zh: 金統軍劉萼聞茨湖敗，亦退師。
units.literal: Jin overall commander Liu E, hearing of the defeat at Cihu, also withdrew his army.
units.idiomatic: Jin commander Liu E, hearing of Cihu's defeat, also withdrew.

units.zh: 王彥遣將閻玘復澠池縣。
units.literal: Wang Yan sent general Yan Qi to recover Mianchi county.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent Yan Qi to retake Mianchi county.

units.zh: 壬寅，天有白氣。
units.literal: Day renyin: white vapor appeared in the sky.
units.idiomatic: On renyin, white vapor appeared in the sky.

units.zh: 戊午，復引兵來攻，撙又敗之，金兵遁去。
units.literal: Day wuwu: they came again; Zong again defeated them and the Jin fled.
units.idiomatic: On wuwu, they returned; Zong defeated them again and the Jin fled.

units.zh: 王彥遣將馬貴斷河中南橋，金兵來攻，貴戰敗之。
units.literal: Wang Yan sent general Ma Gui to cut the south bridge on the Yellow River; the Jin came to attack and Gui defeated them.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent Ma Gui to cut the Yellow River's south bridge; the Jin attacked and Gui defeated them.

units.zh: 壬戌，詔軍士戰死者祿其家一年，傷重而死于營者半之。
units.literal: Day renxu: an edict granted one year's salary to families of soldiers killed in battle; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.
units.idiomatic: On renxu, families of soldiers killed in battle received one year's salary; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.

units.zh: 姚仲遣副將趙銓攻下鎮戎軍，金同知渭州秦弼及其子嵩來歸。
units.literal: Yao Zhong sent deputy Zhao Quan to take Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei prefecture commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song came over.
units.idiomatic: Yao Zhong's deputy Zhao Quan took Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song defected.

units.zh: 王彥遣兵救陝州，遇金人於虢州東，敗之，金兵引去。
units.literal: Wang Yan sent troops to relieve Shan prefecture, met the Jin east of Guo prefecture, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent relief to Shan, met the Jin east of Guo, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.

units.zh: 丁卯，吳珙遣將復永安軍、永寧、福昌、長水三縣。
units.literal: Day dingmao: Wu Gong sent generals to recover Yong'an army and the three counties Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui.
units.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wu Gong's generals retook Yong'an army and Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui counties.

units.zh: 甲辰，罷扈從官吏賞典。
units.literal: Day jiachen: reward grants to officials of the imperial retinue were abolished.
units.idiomatic: On jiachen, reward grants to retinue officials were abolished.

units.zh: 乙巳，錄商、虢之功，加吳璘少傅、王彥為保平軍節度使。
units.literal: Day yisi: the merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was advanced to junior mentor and Wang Yan was made Baoping military commissioner.
units.idiomatic: On yisi, merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was made junior mentor and Wang Yan Baoping military commissioner.

units.zh: 戊申，吳璘復德順軍，又遣將嚴忠取環州。
units.literal: Day wushen: Wu Lin recovered Deshun army and also sent general Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.
units.idiomatic: On wushen, Wu Lin recovered Deshun and sent Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.

title.zh: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝
title.en: Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Hui
title.raw: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Hui

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
units.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.

units.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
units.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.
units.idiomatic: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.

units.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
units.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.
units.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.

units.zh: 三月，平東將軍、齊王冏起兵以討倫，傳檄州郡，屯于陽翟。
units.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Jiong of Qi, raised troops to attack Lun, transmitted proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, and encamped at Yangzhai.
units.idiomatic: In the third month Prince Jiong of Qi, general who pacifies the east, mobilized against Prince Lun, circulated a call to arms through every province, and camped at Yangzhai.

units.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
units.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.
units.idiomatic: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.

units.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
units.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.
units.idiomatic: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.

title.zh: 卷136 齊紀二
title.en: Volume 136 Qi Records 2
title.raw: 卷136 齊紀二

units.zh: 資治通鑑 第136卷
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Government, Volume 136
units.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 136

units.zh: 卷第一百三十六
units.literal: Volume 136
units.idiomatic: Volume 136

units.zh: 【齊紀二】 起閼逢困敦，盡屠維大荒落，凡六年。
units.literal: [Qi Records 2] From Efou Kundun through Tuxi Dahuangluo, six years in all.
units.idiomatic: [Qi Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—six years in all.

units.zh: 魏遣兵擊百濟，為百濟所敗。
units.literal: Wei sent troops to attack Baekje and was defeated by Baekje.
units.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent troops against Baekje and was defeated by them.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明七年（
units.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 7 (
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 7 (

units.zh: 己巳，公元四八九年）
units.literal: jisi, the year 489 CE)
units.idiomatic: jisi, corresponding to 489 CE)

units.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，上祀南郊，大赦。
units.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
units.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty.

units.zh: 壬戌，臨川獻王映卒。
units.literal: On renxu, Prince Xian of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, died.
units.idiomatic: On renxu, Prince Xian of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, died.

units.zh: 初，上為鎮西長史，主簿王晏以傾諂為上所親，自是常在上府。
units.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won the emperor's favor through fawning flattery; from then on he was constantly at the prince's headquarters.
units.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won his favor through sycophantic flattery and thereafter remained constantly at his headquarters.

units.zh: 上為太子，晏為中庶子。
units.literal: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan became Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
units.idiomatic: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan was made Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 上之得罪於太祖也，晏稱疾自疏。
units.literal: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan pleaded illness and kept his distance.
units.idiomatic: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan feigned illness and distanced himself.

units.zh: 及即位，為丹陽尹，意任如舊，朝夕進見，議論朝事；
units.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor's trust in him was as before, and he was received morning and evening to discuss court affairs;
units.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor trusted him as before and received him morning and evening to discuss affairs of state;

units.zh: 自豫章王嶷及王儉皆降意接之。
units.literal: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all lowered themselves to receive him graciously.
units.idiomatic: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all showed deference in receiving him.

units.zh: 二月，壬寅，出為江州刺史；
units.literal: In the second month, on renyin, he was sent out as Inspector of Jiang Province;
units.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, he was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province;

units.zh: 晏不願外出，復留為吏部尚書。
units.literal: Yan did not wish to go out on assignment and was again retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
units.idiomatic: Yan did not wish to leave the capital and was kept on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 三月，甲寅，立皇子子岳為臨賀王，子峻為廣漢王，子琳為宣城王，子鈱為義安王。
units.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.
units.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.

units.zh: 五月，乙巳，儉卒。
units.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, Jian died.
units.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi, Wang Jian died.

units.zh: 王晏既領選，權行台閣，與儉頗不平。
units.literal: Wang Yan, having taken charge of selection, wielded the authority of the Secretariat and was on rather poor terms with Jian.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan, now in charge of personnel selection, exercised the powers of the Secretariat and was on bad terms with Jian.

units.zh: 禮官欲依王導，謚儉為文獻。
units.literal: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and give Jian the posthumous title Literary Paragon.
units.idiomatic: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and posthumously name Jian Literary Paragon.

units.zh: 晏啟上曰：「導乃得此謚；
units.literal: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Dao deserved this posthumous title;
units.idiomatic: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Wang Dao deserved that posthumous title;

units.zh: 但宋氏以來，不加異姓。」
units.literal: since the Song dynasty, such titles have not been granted to those of a different surname;"
units.idiomatic: since the Song, such titles have not been granted to men of a different surname;"

units.zh: 庚戌，魏主祭方澤。
units.literal: On gengxu, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound.
units.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Northern Wei emperor performed the sacrifice at the Square Mound.

units.zh: 上欲用領軍王奐為尚書令，以問王晏。
units.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Wang Yan about it.
units.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Yan.

units.zh: 晏與奐不相能，對曰：「柳世隆有勳望，恐不宜在奐後。」
units.literal: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has merit and prestige; I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."
units.idiomatic: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has both merit and prestige; it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."

units.zh: 甲子，以尚書左僕射柳世隆為尚書令，王奐為左僕射。
units.literal: On jiazi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.
units.idiomatic: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.

title.zh: 卷二十七 列傳第十七 孔靖 孔琳之 殷景仁
title.en: Volume 27 Biographies 17: Kong Jing, Kong Linzhi, Yin Jingren
title.raw: 卷二十七 列傳第十七 孔靖 孔琳之 殷景仁 Volume 27 Biographies 17: Kong Jing, Kong Linzhi, Yin Jingren

units.zh: 列傳第十七
units.literal: Biographies 17
units.idiomatic: the seventeenth year of Biographies

units.zh: 孔靖孔琳之殷景仁
units.literal: Kong Jing, Kong Linzhi, Yin Jingren
units.idiomatic: Kong Jing, Kong Linzhi, Yin Jingren

units.zh: 孔靖字季恭，會稽山陰人也，名與宋武帝祖諱同，故以字稱。
units.literal: Kong Jing, styled Jigong, was from Shanyin in Kuaiji. His personal name was the same as the tabooed name of Emperor Wu of Song's ancestor, so he was referred to by his courtesy name.
units.idiomatic: Kong Jing, whose courtesy name was Jigong, was from Shanyin in Kuaiji. Because his personal name matched the tabooed name of Emperor Wu of Song's ancestor, he was referred to by his courtesy name.

units.zh: 會稽聞西軍稍近，將士多奔亡，覬不能復製。
units.literal: Kuaiji heard the western army drawing near; officers and soldiers mostly fled, and Xi could no longer control them.
units.idiomatic: As imperial forces neared Kuaiji, troops deserted in droves and Xi lost control.

units.zh: 上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，覬憂遽不知所為。
units.literal: The magistrate of Shangyu, Wang Yan, raised troops to attack the commandery; Xi in panic knew not what to do.
units.idiomatic: Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the prefecture; Xi panicked.

units.zh: 其夕率千人聲雲東討，實趨石賜。
units.literal: That evening he led a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern campaign, but in fact hurried to Shici.
units.idiomatic: That night he led a thousand men, claiming an eastern expedition, but fled toward Shici.

units.zh: 遇潮涸不得去，眾叛都盡，門生載以小船，竄於山脊村。
units.literal: The tide ebbed and he could not leave; the masses all rebelled and departed; a student loaded him in a small boat and hid on a mountain ridge village.
units.idiomatic: The tide went out and trapped him; his force melted away; a student rowed him in a skiff to a mountain hamlet.

units.zh: 村人縛以送晏，晏調曰：「此事孔璪所為，無豫卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
units.literal: Villagers bound him and sent him to Yan; Yan jested, "This was Kong Zuan's doing—you had no part; you may compose the chief confession and I will plead for you above."
units.idiomatic: Villagers bound him for Wang Yan, who said lightly, "Kong Zuan did this, not you—write the lead confession and I will speak for you at court."

units.zh: 覬曰：「江東處分，莫不由身，委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
units.literal: Xi said, "Dispositions east of the river all proceed from oneself—to shift guilt and seek life is your kind's way."
units.idiomatic: Xi answered, "Every decision east of the Yang was mine—shift blame to live? That is your trade, not mine."

units.zh: 晏乃斬之東合外。
units.literal: Yan then beheaded him outside the eastern pavilion.
units.idiomatic: Yan beheaded him outside the eastern hall.

units.zh: 臨死求酒，曰：「此是平生所好。」
units.literal: Facing death he asked for wine, saying, "This was my lifelong delight."
units.idiomatic: At the block he asked for wine: "This was my lifelong pleasure."

units.literal: Treatise Eighty-Seven

units.zh: 選舉七
units.literal: Selection and Examinations Seven
units.idiomatic: Selection and Examinations 7

units.zh: 捐納
units.literal: Contribution and Purchase of Office
units.idiomatic: Purchase of Offices

units.zh: 嗣以西安、大同飢，又永定河工，復開事例。
units.literal: Later, because of famine in Xi'an and Datong and Yongding River works, regulations were opened again.
units.idiomatic: Later famine in Xi'an and Datong and works on the Yongding River led to reopening the regulations.

units.zh: 五十一年，增置通州倉廒，科臣有請開捐者，廷議如所請。
units.literal: In the fifty-first year, when granaries at Tongzhou were to be expanded, a censor requested opening contributions; the court deliberated and agreed.
units.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 (1712), when Tongzhou granaries were to be expanded, a censor requested opening contributions, and the court approved.

units.zh: 侍郎王掞抗疏言：「鄉里童騃，一旦捐資，儼然民上。
units.literal: Vice Minister Wang Yan submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Village simpletons, once they contribute funds, suddenly stand above the people.
units.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Yan submitted a forceful memorial: "Country simpletons who pay once suddenly stand above the people they govern.

units.zh: 或分一縣之符，或擁一道之節，不惟濫傷名器，抑且為累地方。
units.literal: Some hold a county's seal, others wield a circuit's authority—not only injuring prestigious titles excessively, but also becoming a burden on local regions.
units.idiomatic: Some hold a county seal, others wield a circuit's authority—this not only debases prestigious ranks but burdens the regions they govern.

units.zh: 宜禁止，以塞僥倖之路，杜言利之門。」
units.literal: It is fitting to forbid this, to block the path of opportunism and shut the door to profit-seeking."
units.idiomatic: It should be forbidden, to block opportunism and shut the door to profiteering."

units.zh: 帝韙之，為飭九卿再議。
units.literal: The emperor approved this and ordered the Nine Ministers to deliberate again.
units.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the Nine Ministers to reconsider.

units.zh: 青海用兵，饋餉不繼，內大臣議停各途守選及遷補，專用捐資助餉者。
units.literal: When Qinghai was at war and supplies did not keep up, inner ministers proposed halting selection and transfer along all routes and using only those who contributed funds to aid supplies.
units.idiomatic: During the Qinghai campaign, when supplies ran short, inner ministers proposed suspending normal selection and transfers and relying solely on contributors to fund the army.

title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第四十一 孫惠 熊遠 王鑒 陳頵 高崧 Volume 71 Biographies 41: Sun Hui; Xiong Yuan; Wang Jian; Chen Yun; Gao Song

units.zh: 孫惠
units.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.
units.idiomatic: Sun Hui.

units.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。
units.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.
units.idiomatic: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.

units.zh: 父祖並仕吳。
units.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.
units.idiomatic: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.

units.zh: 文集傳於世。
units.literal: His collected writings circulated in the age.
units.idiomatic: His literary collection survived him in circulation.

units.zh: 鑒弟濤及弟子戭，並有才筆。
units.literal: Jian's younger brother Tao and his nephew Yan both had talent with the brush.
units.idiomatic: His brother Wang Tao and his nephew Wang Yan were both fine writers.

units.zh: 濤字茂略，曆著作郎、無錫令。
units.literal: Tao, courtesy name Maolue, successively served as editorial director and magistrate of Wuxi.
units.idiomatic: Wang Tao, courtesy Maolue, rose through editorial director to magistrate of Wuxi.

units.zh: 戭字庭堅，亦為著作。
units.literal: Yan, courtesy name Tingjian, also served as editorial director.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan, courtesy Tingjian, also held a compiler's post.

units.zh: 並早卒。
units.literal: Both died early.
units.idiomatic: Both died young.

units.zh: 陳頵
units.literal: Section heading: Chen Yun.
units.idiomatic: Chen Yun.

units.zh: 太祖三
units.literal: Taizu III.
units.idiomatic: Annals of Taizu, continued.

units.zh: 五年春正月壬辰朔，雨雪，不御殿。
units.literal: In year five, spring, first month, on renchen, the new-moon day, rain and snow fell; he did not hold audience in the main hall.
units.idiomatic: In Kaibao year five, on the renchen new moon in the first month of spring, snow mixed with rain, and he withheld court audience.

units.zh: 禁鐵鑄浮屠及佛像。
units.literal: Iron was forbidden for casting stupas and Buddha images.
units.idiomatic: He banned the use of iron to cast pagodas and Buddha statues.

units.zh: 丁酉，命吳越王錢俶為昇州東南行營招撫制置使。
units.literal: On dingyou, Wuyue king Qian Chu was made pacification and disposition commissioner of the Southeast Route Army for Shengzhou.
units.idiomatic: On dingyou King Qian Chu of Wuyue was named pacification commissioner on the southeastern front against Shengzhou.

units.zh: 己亥，曹彬收下峽口，獲指揮使王仁震、王宴、錢興。
units.literal: On jihai, Cao Bin took Xiakou and captured commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing.
units.idiomatic: On jihai Cao Bin seized Xiakou and took commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing prisoner.

units.zh: 閏月己酉，克池州。
units.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiyou, Chizhou was taken.
units.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiyou, the army captured Chizhou.

title.zh: 卷三百九十五 列傳第一百五十四 樓鑰 李大性 任希夷 徐應龍 莊夏 王阮 王質 陸游 方信孺 王柟
title.en: Volume 395 Biographies 154: Lou Yao, Li Daxing, Ren Xiyi, Xu Yinglong, Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, Wang Zhi, Lu You, Fang Xinru, Wang Nan
title.raw: 卷三百九十五 列傳第一百五十四 樓鑰 李大性 任希夷 徐應龍 莊夏 王阮 王質 陸游 方信孺 王柟 Volume 395 Biographies 154: Lou Yao, Li Daxing, Ren Xiyi, Xu Yinglong, Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, Wang Zhi, Lu You, Fang Xinru, Wang Nan

units.zh: 樓鑰，字大防，明州鄞縣人。
units.literal: Lou Yao, styled Dafang, was a native of Yin County in Ming Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Lou Yao, courtesy name Dafang, came from Yin County in Mingzhou.

units.zh: 隆興元年，試南宮，有司偉其辭藝，欲以冠多士，策偶犯舊諱，知貢舉洪遵奏，得旨以冠末等。
units.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he tested at the Southern Palace examination; the officials admired his literary skill and wished to place him first among the successful candidates, but his policy essay accidentally violated an old taboo name; Hong Zun, the chief examiner, memorialized, and he received the imperial decision to be ranked last among the top tier.
units.idiomatic: In Longxing 1 (1163), he sat for the metropolitan examination. The examiners admired his writing and intended to rank him first, but his policy essay inadvertently violated an old naming taboo. Chief examiner Hong Zun reported this, and by imperial order Lou was placed last among the highest tier of graduates.

units.zh: 投贄謝諸公，考官胡銓稱之曰：「此翰林才也。」
units.literal: Presenting a letter of thanks to the examiners, the examiner Hu Quan praised him, saying: "This is talent fit for the Hanlin Academy."
units.idiomatic: When he submitted a letter of thanks to the examiners, Hu Quan, one of the examiners, praised him: "This man has the makings of a Hanlin academician."

units.zh: 久之，通判夔州。
units.literal: After a long time he was made vice prefect of Kuizhou.
units.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made vice prefect of Kuizhou.

units.zh: 王炎宣撫川、陝，辟為幹辦公事。
units.literal: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Chuan and Shan and recruited him as administrative officer.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi and recruited him as administrative officer.

units.zh: 游為炎陳進取之策，以為經略中原必自長安始，取長安必自隴右始。
units.literal: You presented Yan a strategy of advance, holding that to plan the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.
units.idiomatic: You presented Yan a strategy of advance: to recover the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.

units.zh: 當積粟練兵，有釁則攻，無則守。
units.literal: One should accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when there is an opening, defend when there is none.
units.idiomatic: Accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when opportunity opens, defend when it does not.

units.zh: 吳璘子挺代掌兵，頗驕恣，傾財結士，屢以過誤殺人，炎莫誰何。
units.literal: Wu Lin's son Ting took command of the army, quite arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win over scholars, repeatedly killing men through errors — Yan could do nothing.
units.idiomatic: Wu Lin's son Ting took command, arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win scholars and repeatedly killing men through negligence — Yan could not restrain him.

units.zh: 游請以玠子拱代挺。
units.literal: You asked that Jie's son Gong replace Ting.
units.idiomatic: You asked that Wu Jie's son Gong replace Ting.

units.zh: 炎曰：「拱怯而寡謀，遇敵必敗。」
units.literal: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; meeting the enemy he will surely be defeated."
units.idiomatic: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; he will surely be defeated."

units.zh: 游曰：「使挺遇敵，安保其不敗。
units.literal: You said: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?
units.idiomatic: You replied: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?

title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁 Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren

units.zh: 列傳第五十三
units.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three
units.idiomatic: the 53th year of Biographies

units.zh: 王神念羊侃羊鴉仁
units.literal: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
units.idiomatic: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, and Yang Ren

units.zh: 王神念，太原祁人也。
units.literal: Wang Shennian was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
units.idiomatic: Wang Shennian was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 初，僧辯平建鄴，遣陳武守京口，推以赤心，結廉、藺之分。
units.literal: Earlier, when Senbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Chen Wu to guard Jingkou, extending with a red heart, forming the bond of Lian and Lin.
units.idiomatic: After Senbian pacified Jiankang, he placed Chen Wu at Jingkou in the trust of sworn friendship, like Lian Po and Lin Xiangru.

units.zh: 且為第三子頠許娶陳武章後所生女，未昏而僧辯母亡，然情好甚密，其長子顗屢諫不聽。
units.literal: Moreover he betrothed his third son Yi to the daughter born to Chen Wu's wife Zhang; before marriage Senbian's mother died, yet their affection was very close; his eldest son Yan repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded.
units.idiomatic: He even betrothed his third son Yi to Chen Wu's daughter by Lady Zhang; though Senbian's mother died before the wedding, the two remained intimate, despite repeated warnings from his eldest son Yan.

units.zh: 至是，會江淮人報云：「齊兵大舉至壽春」，僧辯謂齊軍必出江表，因遣記室參軍江旰以事報陳武，仍使整舟艦器械。
units.literal: At this point, a person from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops in great force have reached Shouchun"; Senbian thought Qi army would surely come out onto the Jiang region, and therefore sent Recorder of the Headquarters Jiang Gan to report the matter to Chen Wu, still ordering him to put ships and weapons in order.
units.idiomatic: Just then a man from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops are massing at Shouchun"; Senbian assumed they would cross the Yangtze and sent his secretary Jiang Gan to inform Chen Wu and prepare the fleet.

units.zh: 乃敢進，遂克之，時壽春竟無齊軍，又非陳武之譎，殆天授也。
units.literal: Only then did he dare advance, and thus captured it; at the time Shouchun ultimately had no Qi army, and it was not Chen Wu's stratagem—perhaps heaven conferred it.
units.idiomatic: Only then did he advance and take the city; as it happened there were no Qi troops at Shouchun at all—it was no ruse of Chen Wu's, but almost as if heaven had granted him the moment.

units.zh: 顗承聖初位侍中，魏克江陵，隨王琳入齊，為竟陵郡守。
units.literal: Yan in the beginning of Chengsheng held Palace Attendant; when Wei took Jiangling, he followed Wang Lin into Qi and served as Administrator of Jingling Commandery.
units.idiomatic: Yan became Palace Attendant early in the Chengsheng era; when Wei conquered Jiangling he went north with Wang Lin and served as governor of Jingling.

units.zh: 齊遣王琳鎮壽春，將圖江左。
units.literal: Qi dispatched Wang Lin to garrison Shouchun, intending to scheme against the Jiang left bank.
units.idiomatic: Qi sent Wang Lin to hold Shouchun, aiming to reconquer the south.

units.zh: 及陳平淮南殺琳，顗聞之，乃出郡城南登高塚上，號哭一慟而絕。
units.literal: When Chen pacified Huainan and killed Lin, Yan heard of it; he then went south of the commandery city and climbed a high mound, wailing one great grief and expiring.
units.idiomatic: When Chen conquered Huainan and killed Wang Lin, Yan climbed a mound south of the city, gave one great cry of grief, and died on the spot.

units.zh: 顗弟頒，少有志節，恒隨梁元帝。
units.literal: Yan's younger brother Ban, from youth had aspiration and integrity, always following Liang Emperor Yuan.
units.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Ban was spirited from youth and always followed Emperor Yuan of Liang.

units.zh: 資治通鑑 第136卷
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Government, Volume 136
units.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 136

units.zh: 卷第一百三十六
units.literal: Volume 136
units.idiomatic: Volume 136

units.zh: 【齊紀二】 起閼逢困敦，盡屠維大荒落，凡六年。
units.literal: [Qi Records 2] From Efou Kundun through Tuxi Dahuangluo, six years in all.
units.idiomatic: [Qi Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—six years in all.

units.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，難之，終不能屈。
units.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and countryside clamored; many challenged it, but in the end none could overcome him.
units.idiomatic: When the treatise appeared, court and country were in an uproar; critics assailed it, but none could refute him in the end.

units.zh: 太原王琰著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼范子！
units.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise to mock Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen: "Alas, Master Fan!

units.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在！」
units.literal: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"
units.idiomatic: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"

units.zh: 欲以杜縝後對。
units.literal: He wished thereby to block Zhen from replying.
units.idiomatic: He meant to silence any reply from Zhen.

units.zh: 縝對曰：「嗚呼王子！
units.literal: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!
units.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

units.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」
units.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"
units.idiomatic: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"

title.zh: 卷九十九 漢書1: 高祖本紀上
title.en: Volume 99 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1
title.raw: 卷九十九 漢書1: 高祖本紀上 Volume 99 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1

units.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，姓劉氏，諱暠，本名知遠，及即位改今諱。
units.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Sacred, Martial, Illustrious, and Solemnly Filial Emperor, bore the surname Liu; his taboo name was Gao; his original name was Zhiyuan, which upon his accession he changed to the present taboo name.
units.idiomatic: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Sacred, Martial, Illustrious, and Solemnly Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan; his taboo name was Gao. He had been born Zhiyuan and took the present taboo name when he came to the throne.

units.zh: 其先本沙陀部人也。
units.literal: His ancestors were originally people of the Shatuo tribe.
units.idiomatic: His forebears were originally of the Shatuo tribe.

units.zh: 四代祖諱湍，帝有天下，追尊為明元皇帝，廟號文祖，陵曰懿陵；
units.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor was named Tuan; after the Emperor possessed All Under Heaven, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan, with temple name Wenzu and tomb called Yiling;
units.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor was named Tuan; once the emperor held the realm, Tuan was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan, with the temple name Wenzu and the tomb Yiling;

units.zh: 自是群官三上箋，諸軍將吏、緇黃耆耋，相次迫請，教答允之。
units.literal: From then on the officials submitted memorials three times; military officers, monks and priests, and elders in succession pressed the request, and an edict in reply agreed.
units.idiomatic: Thereafter officials memorialized three times, and officers, clergy, and elders pressed him in turn until an edict in reply accepted.

units.zh: 庚午，陜府屯駐奉國指揮使趙暉、侯章、都頭王晏殺契丹監軍及副使劉願，暉自稱留後。
units.literal: On the day gengwu Zhao Hui, commander of the Fengguo army stationed at Shaan prefecture, Hou Zhang, and company head Wang Yan killed the Khitan military supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui styled himself acting military governor.
units.idiomatic: On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui declared himself acting military governor.

units.zh: 契丹因授暉陜州兵馬留後，侯章為本州馬步軍都指揮使，王晏為副都指揮使，暉等不受命。
units.literal: The Khitan thereupon appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander; Hui and the others did not accept the appointments.
units.idiomatic: The Khitan then appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander, but they refused the orders.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·王晏傳》：開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。
units.literal: (Song History, Biography of Wang Yan: At the end of Kaiyun he garrisoned Shaanzhou with the army commander Zhao Hui, the Zhongwei commander Hou Zhang, and others.
units.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Wang Yan: At the end of Kaiyun he was posted to Shaanzhou with Zhao Hui, commander of the main force, Hou Zhang of the Zhongwei guard, and others.

units.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉願據陜，恣行暴虐。
units.literal: It happened that the Khitan reached Bian and sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, who indulged in violence and cruelty.
units.idiomatic: When the Khitan reached Bian they sent Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, and he ravaged the people.

units.zh: 晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。
units.literal: Yan plotted with Hui and the others, saying: "Now the Khitan invade the south and the realm is in turmoil; heroes and great men ought surely to seize the moment and rouse themselves.
units.idiomatic: Yan said to Hui and the others, "The Khitan are invading the south and the realm is in uproar; men of spirit ought to seize the moment.

units.zh: 且聞太原劉公，威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺願送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳！」
units.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige and virtue extend far and men's hearts submit to him; if we kill Yuan and send allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then winning wealth and rank will be like turning the hand!"
units.idiomatic: We hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's fame reaches far and the people look to him. If we kill Yuan and submit to Hedong, leading the realm, wealth and rank will come as easily as turning one's hand!"

units.zh: 暉等然之。
units.literal: Hui and the others agreed.
units.idiomatic: Hui and the others agreed.

units.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人，夜逾城入府署，劫庫兵給其徒。
units.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men, by night scaled the wall and entered the government compound, seized arms from the arsenal and supplied his followers.
units.idiomatic: Yan led a few daredevils over the wall by night into the government compound, seized weapons from the arsenal, and armed his men.

units.zh: 遲明，斬願首懸府門外。
units.literal: At dawn he beheaded Yuan and hung the head outside the government gate.
units.idiomatic: At dawn they beheaded Yuan and hung his head outside the gate.

units.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候，乃遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。）〉
units.literal: The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉
units.idiomatic: The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉

units.zh: 辛未，帝於太原宮受冊，即皇帝位，制改晉開運四年為天福十二年。
units.literal: On the day xinwei the Emperor received the seal at the Taiyuan palace, ascended the imperial throne, and by edict changed Jin's fourth year of Kaiyun to the twelfth year of Tianfu.
units.idiomatic: On xinwei he received the seal at the Taiyuan palace and took the throne, renaming Jin's fourth year of Kaiyun as the twelfth year of Tianfu.

units.zh: 趙延壽於鎮州自稱權知國事。
units.literal: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou styled himself acting administrator of state affairs.
units.idiomatic: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou declared himself acting administrator of state affairs.

units.zh: 辛巳，陜州節度使趙暉加檢校太尉，華州節度使兼陜州馬步軍都指揮使侯章加檢校太傅，以陜府馬步軍副都指揮使兼絳州防禦使王晏為晉州節度使、檢校太傅，以丹州都指揮使、權知軍州事高彥珣為丹州刺史。
units.literal: On the day xinsi Zhao Hui, military governor of Shaanzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal; Hou Zhang, military governor of Huazhou and Commander-in-Chief of Shaanzhou's cavalry and infantry, was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor; Wang Yan, vice commander of Shaan prefecture's horse and foot and Defender of Jiangzhou, was made military governor of Jinzhou and Acting Grand Tutor; and Gao Yanqi, commander of Danzhou and acting administrator of military and prefectural affairs, was made Prefect of Danzhou.
units.idiomatic: On xinsi Zhao Hui was made Acting Grand Marshal, Hou Zhang Acting Grand Tutor, Wang Yan military governor of Jinzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, and Gao Yanqi prefect of Danzhou.

units.zh: 劉皞，字克明，晉丞相譙國公句之弟也。
units.literal: Liu Hao, courtesy name Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.
units.idiomatic: Liu Hao, whose courtesy name was Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.

units.zh: 句，《晉書》有傳。
units.literal: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.
units.idiomatic: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.

units.zh: 皞少離鄉里，唐天祐中，梁將劉鄩襲太原，軍至樂平，時皞客於縣舍，為鄩軍所俘。
units.literal: Hao left his native place while still young. In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun raided Taiyuan; when the army reached Leping, Hao was lodging at the county guesthouse and was captured by Xun's troops.
units.idiomatic: Hao had left his hometown while still young. During the Tianyou reign of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun attacked Taiyuan; when his army reached Leping, Hao was staying at the county inn and was taken prisoner by Xun's forces.

units.zh: 後繼歷州縣，歷仕晉、漢、周，官至工部尚書。
units.literal: He later successively served in prefectures and counties, held office through Jin, Han, and Zhou, and reached the post of minister of Works.
units.idiomatic: He later served in successive county and prefectural posts, held office under Jin, Han, and Zhou, and rose to minister of Works.

units.zh: 王延，字世美，鄚州長豐人也。
units.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Mozhou.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan, whose courtesy name was Shimei, came from Changfeng in Mozhou.

units.zh: 少為儒，善詞賦，會鄉曲離亂，不獲從鄉薦，因客於浮陽，隨滄帥戴思遠入梁。
units.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar, skilled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home district was torn by disorder he could not obtain local recommendation, and therefore lodged in Fuyang, following the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang.
units.idiomatic: In youth he studied the classics and excelled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home region fell into chaos he could not obtain a local recommendation, so he lodged in Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang service.

units.zh: 嘗以所為賦謁梁相李琪，琪覽之，欣然曰：「此道近難其人，王生升我堂矣。」
units.literal: He once presented a fu he had written to the Liang chancellor Li Qi; Qi read it and said with pleasure, "In recent times this art has lacked its master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my hall."
units.idiomatic: He once presented a fu he had written to Liang Chancellor Li Qi, who read it and said with delight, "This art has lately lacked a true master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my level."

units.zh: 繇是人士稱之。
units.literal: From this men of letters praised him.
units.idiomatic: From that time men of letters spoke highly of him.

units.zh: 尋薦為即墨縣令，歷徐、宋、鄆、青四鎮從事。
units.literal: Soon he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and successively served as aide in the four circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.
units.idiomatic: He was soon recommended as magistrate of Jimo and went on to serve as aide in the Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing circuits.

units.zh: 長興初，鄉人馮道、趙鳳在相位，擢拜左補闕。
units.literal: At the beginning of Changxing his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held the chief ministership; he was promoted and appointed left supplementer.
units.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were chief ministers; he was promoted to left supplementer.

units.zh: 逾年，以水部員外知制誥遷中書舍人，賜金紫。
units.literal: After a year he was transferred from vice director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and was granted gold-and-purple.
units.idiomatic: A year later he moved from vice director of the Water Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and received the gold-and-purple insignia.

units.zh: 時有舉子崔頎者，故相協之子也。
units.literal: At the time there was an examinee named Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.
units.idiomatic: Among the candidates was Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.

units.zh: 協素與吏部尚書盧文紀不睦，及延將入貢院，文紀謂延曰：「舍人以謹重聞於時，所以去冬老夫在相位時，與諸相首以長者聞奏，用掌文衡。
units.literal: Xie had long been on bad terms with the minister of Personnel Lu Wenji; as Yan was about to enter the examination compound, Wenji said to him, "You, Drafter, are known in the age for caution and weight; therefore last winter, when this old man was chief minister, I reported first among the ministers that a man of mature reputation should be appointed to hold the literary scales.
units.idiomatic: Xie had long been at odds with Minister of Personnel Lu Wenji. As Yan was about to enter the examination hall, Wenji told him, "You are known for your caution and gravity; that is why last winter, when I was chief minister, I was the first among the ministers to recommend a man of mature reputation to oversee the examinations.

units.zh: 然貢闈取士，頗多面目。
units.literal: Yet in selecting scholars in the examination compound, there are often many personal connections.
units.idiomatic: Yet in selecting candidates for the examinations, personal connections often play a large part.

units.zh: 舍人當求實才，以副公望。」
units.literal: You, Drafter, ought to seek real talent, to fulfill public expectation.
units.idiomatic: You, as Drafter, should seek genuine talent to live up to the reputation you enjoy."

units.zh: 延退而謂人曰：「盧公之言，蓋為崔頎也。
units.literal: Yan withdrew and said to others, "Master Lu's words were surely aimed at Cui Qi.
units.idiomatic: Yan withdrew and told others, "Master Lu's remarks were surely directed at Cui Qi.

units.zh: 縱與其父不悅，致意何至此耶！」
units.literal: Even if he was displeased with the man's father, why carry the hint to such an extent!
units.idiomatic: Even if he bore ill will toward the boy's father, why make his meaning so plain!"

units.zh: 其年，改御史中丞，歲滿，轉尚書右丞。
units.literal: That year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.
units.idiomatic: That same year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and when his term ended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.

units.zh: 奉使兩浙，吳人深重之。
units.literal: On a mission to the Two Zhes, the people of Wu held him in deep esteem.
units.idiomatic: While serving as envoy to the Two Zhes, he won the deep respect of the people of Wu.

units.zh: 復命，授吏部侍郎，改尚書左丞，拜太常卿，歷工、禮、刑三尚書。
units.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and served successively as Minister of Works, Rites, and Punishments.
units.idiomatic: After reporting back, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and went on to hold the ministries of Works, Rites, and Punishments in succession.

units.zh: 以疾求分司西洛，授太子少保。
units.literal: Citing illness, he requested a post in the western Luoyang branch office and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
units.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and asked for a post in the Luoyang branch office in the west, and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 既而連月請告，為留臺所糾，改少傅致仕。
units.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly took leave for months on end and was censured by the Luoyang branch office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor and retired.
units.idiomatic: Before long he took medical leave month after month, was censured by the Luoyang branch office, and was reassigned as Junior Preceptor before retiring from office.

units.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，時年七十有三。
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-three.
units.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun, at the age of seventy-three.

units.zh: 子億，仕皇朝為殿中丞。
units.literal: His son Yi served the present dynasty as Director in the Palace Bureau.
units.idiomatic: His son Yi served the present dynasty as a Director in the Palace Bureau.

units.zh: 申文炳，字國華，洛陽人也。
units.literal: Shen Wenbing, courtesy name Guohua, was a native of Luoyang.
units.idiomatic: Shen Wenbing, whose courtesy name was Guohua, was a native of Luoyang.

units.zh: 趙暉，字重光，澶州人也。
units.literal: Zhao Hui, style name Chongguang, was a man of Chanzhou.
units.idiomatic: Zhao Hui, whose style was Chongguang, was a native of Chanzhou.

units.zh: 弱冠以驍果應募，始隸於莊宗帳前，與大梁兵經百餘戰，以功遷馬直軍使。
units.literal: Upon reaching manhood he enlisted in the valiant corps, first serving under Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard; he fought the armies of Great Liang in more than a hundred engagements and was promoted to commander of the horse guard for his merit.
units.idiomatic: When he came of age he joined the elite shock troops and was first assigned to Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard. He fought the armies of Later Liang in more than a hundred battles and, for his achievements, was promoted to commander of the imperial horse guard.

units.zh: 同光中，從魏王破蜀，命暉分統所部，南戍蠻陬。
units.literal: During the Tongguang era he followed the Prince of Wei in the conquest of Shu; Hui was ordered to take separate command of his unit and garrison the southern frontier against the barbarians.
units.idiomatic: During the Tongguang reign he accompanied the Prince of Wei in the campaign that conquered Shu. He was then ordered to lead his own detachment south to guard the frontier against the southern tribes.

units.zh: 開運末，以部兵屯於陜，屬契丹入汴，慨然有憤激之意。
units.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era he stationed his troops at Shaan; when the Khitans entered Bian, he was stirred by indignant resolve.
units.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyun reign he encamped his division at Shaan. When the Khitans entered Bian, he was filled with angry determination.

units.zh: 及聞漢祖建義於並門，乃與部將王晏、侯章戮力葉謀，逐契丹所命官屬，據有陜州，即時馳騎聞於漢祖。
units.literal: When he heard that the Han founder had raised the banner of righteousness at Bing Gate, he joined his subordinate commanders Wang Yan and Hou Zhang in concerted plotting, expelled the officials appointed by the Khitans, seized Shaan prefecture, and at once dispatched riders to report to the Han founder.
units.idiomatic: Learning that the founder of Later Han had raised his standard at Taiyuan, he plotted together with his officers Wang Yan and Hou Zhang, drove out the officials the Khitans had installed, took control of Shaan prefecture, and immediately sent horsemen to inform the Han founder.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹主賜趙暉詔，即以為保義留後。
units.literal: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan ruler issued an edict to Zhao Hui and at once appointed him acting military governor of Baoyi.
units.idiomatic: (According to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan emperor issued an edict to Zhao Hui and immediately appointed him acting military governor of Baoyi.

units.zh: 白時中 徐處仁 馮澥 王倫 宇文虛中 湯思退
units.literal: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, Tang Situi
units.idiomatic: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, and Tang Situi

units.zh: 白時中
units.literal: Bai Shizhong
units.idiomatic: Bai Shizhong

units.zh: 白時中，字蒙亨，壽春人。
units.literal: Bai Shizhong, style name Menghui, was a native of Shouchun.
units.idiomatic: Bai Shizhong, whose style name was Menghui, came from Shouchun.

units.zh: 既而金專事殺戮，上意中悔，思退復密令孫造諭敵以重兵脅和。
units.literal: Before long the Jin devoted themselves to slaughter; the emperor's heart midway regretted; Situi again secretly had Sun Zao tell the enemy to coerce peace with heavy troops.
units.idiomatic: When the Jin turned to slaughter the emperor regretted it; Situi secretly had Sun Zao tell them to coerce peace with heavy troops.

units.zh: 上聞有敵兵，命建康都統王彥等禦之，仍命思退督江、淮軍，辭不行。
units.literal: When the emperor heard of enemy troops he ordered Jiankang Commander Wang Yan and others to resist, and also ordered Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined and would not go.
units.idiomatic: Hearing of enemy troops, the emperor ordered Wang Yan to resist and Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined.

units.zh: 僕散忠義自清河口渡淮，言者極論思退急和撤備之罪，遂罷相，尋責居永州。
units.literal: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; remonstrators fiercely criticized Situi for urgently seeking peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed as chancellor and soon banished to Yongzhou.
units.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; critics attacked Situi for rushing peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed and banished to Yongzhou.

units.zh: 淮河泇河衛河漳河沁河滹沱河桑乾河膠萊河
units.literal: Huai River, Jia River, Wei River, Zhang River, Qin River, Hutuo River, Sanggan River, Jiao-Lai River.
units.idiomatic: The Huai River; the Jia River; the Wei River; the Zhang River; the Qin River; the Hutuo River; the Sanggan River; the Jiao-Lai River.

units.zh: 淮河，出河南平氏胎簪山。
units.literal: The Huai River rises from Mount Taizan in Pingshi, Henan.
units.idiomatic: The Huai River has its source at Mount Taizan in Pingshi, Henan.

units.zh: 經桐伯，其流始大。
units.literal: Passing Tongbo, its flow first becomes large.
units.idiomatic: After passing Tongbo, its current first grows substantial.

units.zh: 若引沁入衛，則張秋無患。」
units.literal: If lead Qin enter Wei, then Zhangqiu no worry."
units.idiomatic: If the Qin were led into the Wei, Zhangqiu would be spared further trouble."

units.zh: 行人王晏亦言：「開岡頭置閘，分沁水，使南入黃，北達衛。
units.literal: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou place locks, divide Qin water, make south enter Yellow, north reach Wei.
units.idiomatic: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou and install locks to divide the Qin so that one branch flows south into the Yellow River and another north to the Wei.

units.zh: 遇漲則閉閘，漕可永無患。」
units.literal: Encounter flood then close locks, grain transport can forever no worry."
units.idiomatic: When the waters rise, close the locks, and the grain transport will never again be in danger."

units.zh: 既而罷引沁河議。
units.literal: Soon after abandoned draw Qin River proposal.
units.idiomatic: Soon afterward the plan to divert the Qin was dropped.

units.zh: 初，王晏請漕沁，有司多言弗利。
units.literal: Initially, Wang Yan requested grain transport Qin, responsible officials many spoke not advantageous.
units.idiomatic: At first, when Wang Yan proposed using the Qin for grain transport, many local officers said it would not pay.

units.zh: 晏固爭。
units.literal: Yan firmly contended.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan pressed his case stubbornly.

units.zh: 吏部尚書王直請遣官行河，命侍郎趙榮同晏往。
units.literal: Ministry of Personnel Minister Wang Zhi requested send officials travel river, ordered Vice Minister Zhao Rong together with Yan go.
units.idiomatic: Minister Wang Zhi of the Ministry of Personnel asked that officials be sent to survey the river, and Vice Minister Zhao Rong was ordered to go with Wang Yan.

units.zh: 榮亦言不利，議乃寢。
units.literal: Rong also spoke not advantageous, proposal then shelved.
units.idiomatic: Zhao Rong also reported that it would not work, and the plan was shelved.

units.zh: 王秀之 王慈 蔡約 陸慧曉 顧憲之 蕭惠基
units.literal: Wang Xiuzhi, Wang Ci, Cai Yue, Lu Huixiao, Gu Xianzhi, Xiao Huiji
units.idiomatic: Wang Xiuzhi · Wang Ci · Cai Yue · Lu Huixiao · Gu Xianzhi · Xiao Huiji

units.zh: 王秀之字伯奮，琅邪臨沂人也。
units.literal: Wang Xiuzhi, style name Bo Fen, was a native of Langya, Linyi.
units.idiomatic: Wang Xiuzhi, whose style name was Bo Fen, came from Langya commandery in Linyi.

units.zh: 慈議不行。
units.literal: Ci's proposal was not adopted.
units.idiomatic: Ci's proposal was not adopted.

units.zh: 慈患脚，世祖敕王晏曰：「慈在職未久，旣有微疾，不堪朝，又不能騎馬，聽乘車在仗後。」
units.literal: Ci suffered from foot ailment; Emperor Shizu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long been in office and already has a slight illness—he cannot manage court, and also cannot ride horseback; allow him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."
units.idiomatic: Ci suffered from foot ailment. Emperor Wu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long held office and already has a slight illness—he cannot attend court and cannot ride horseback; permit him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."

units.zh: 江左來少例也。
units.literal: Since the Eastern Jin such cases have been few.
units.idiomatic: Such indulgence had been rare since the Eastern Jin.

units.zh: 俄徵黃門郎，未拜，遷吏部郎。
units.literal: Soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates; before taking appointment, transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
units.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, but before taking up the appointment he was transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 尚書令王晏選門生補內外要局，慧曉爲用數人而止，晏恨之。
units.literal: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, selected his disciples to fill key posts inside and outside; Huixiao used only a few and stopped—Yan resented this.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, wanted his disciples appointed to key posts throughout the government; Huixiao appointed only a few and stopped, and Yan resented him for it.

units.zh: 送女妓一人，欲與申好，慧曉不納。
units.literal: Yan sent one female entertainer, wishing to establish goodwill; Huixiao did not accept.
units.idiomatic: Yan sent him a female entertainer hoping to win his favor, but Huixiao refused the gift.

units.zh: 蕭景先
units.literal: Xiao Jingxian
units.idiomatic: Xiao Jingxian

units.zh: 蕭景先，南蘭陵蘭陵人，太祖從子也。
units.literal: Xiao Jingxian was a man of Lanling in Nan Lanling, a cousin's son of the Grand Progenitor.
units.idiomatic: Xiao Jingxian was a native of Lanling in Nan Lanling, a cousin's son of Emperor Gao.

units.zh: 祖爰之，員外郎。
units.literal: His grandfather Aizhi was Outer Gentleman-attendant.
units.idiomatic: His grandfather Aizhi had served as Outer Gentleman-attendant.

units.zh: 毅性奢豪，好弓馬，爲高宗所疑忌。
units.literal: Yi's nature was extravagant and proud; he loved bow and horse and was suspected and envied by Emperor Ming.
units.idiomatic: Yi was extravagant by nature and loved archery and horsemanship; Emperor Ming came to view him with suspicion.

units.zh: 王晏事敗，幷陷誅之。
units.literal: When Wang Yan's affair failed, Yi was implicated and executed with him.
units.idiomatic: When Wang Yan's plot failed, Yi was implicated and executed along with him.

units.zh: 遣軍圍宅，毅時會賔客奏伎，聞變，索刀未得，收人突進，挾持毅入與母別，出便殺之。
units.literal: Troops were sent to surround the residence; Yi at the time was hosting guests with performers playing; hearing the change, he sought a knife but did not obtain it; arresters burst in, seized Yi and brought him in to part from his mother, and once outside killed him at once.
units.idiomatic: Troops were sent to surround his house while he was entertaining guests with music. When he heard what was happening he reached for a knife but could not find one; the arresters burst in, took him in to bid his mother farewell, and killed him as soon as they led him out.

units.zh: 賜穎冑以常所乘白＜牜俞＞牛。
units.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yingzhou the white riding ox he habitually used.
units.idiomatic: The emperor gave Yingzhou the white ox he habitually rode.

units.zh: 上慕儉約，欲鑄壞太官元日上壽銀酒鎗，尚書令王晏等咸稱盛德。
units.literal: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Minister Over the Masses Wang Yan and others all praised this as supreme virtue.
units.idiomatic: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Wang Yan, Minister Over the Masses, and others all praised this as supreme virtue.

units.zh: 穎冑曰：「朝廷盛禮，莫過三元。
units.literal: Yingzhou said: "Among the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.
units.idiomatic: Yingzhou said: "Of all the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.

units.zh: 志第十三 天文一
units.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1
units.idiomatic: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One

units.zh: 言天者有三家，一曰宣夜，二曰蓋天，三曰渾天，而天之正體，經無前說，馬《書》、班《志》，又闕其文。
units.literal: Those who speak of Heaven belong to three schools: first Xuanye, second Gaitian, third Huntian; yet Heaven's true form has no prior exposition in the classics, and in Ma Rong's commentary and Ban Gu's treatise the text is likewise missing.
units.idiomatic: Writers on the cosmos fall into three traditions—Xuanye, Gaitian, and Huntian—yet the classics never settled the true shape of the sky, and neither Ma Rong's Shangshu commentary nor Ban Gu's astronomical monograph preserves an earlier account.

units.zh: 漢靈帝議郎蔡邕于朔方上書曰：「論天體者三家，宣夜之學，絕無師法。
units.literal: Consultation Gentleman Cai Yong of Emperor Ling of Han, writing from Shuofang, submitted a memorial saying: "Those who discuss the celestial body are three schools; the learning of Xuanye has absolutely no teachers or transmitted method.
units.idiomatic: From exile in Shuofang, Cai Yong—Consultation Gentleman under Emperor Ling of Han—wrote: "Cosmology had three schools, but the Xuanye tradition had no living teachers and no line of transmission.

units.zh: 占曰：「犯昴，胡不安。」
units.literal: Prognostication says: "Encroaching on Hairy Head means the northern tribes are unsettled".
units.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Striking Hairy Head foretells unrest among the northern peoples".

units.zh: 二年六月，鮮卑阿妙兒等寇西方，燉煌太守王延斬之，并二千餘級。
units.literal: " Year 2, sixth month: the Xianbei led by Amiao'er and others raided the west; Wang Yan, Administrator of Dunhuang, beheaded them, more than two thousand heads in all.
units.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year two the Xianbei under Amiao'er raided the west; Dunhuang administrator Wang Yan killed them, taking more than two thousand heads.

units.zh: 三年，又斬鮮卑大帥及千餘級。
units.literal: Year 3: the Xianbei great chief was again beheaded, with more than a thousand heads.
units.idiomatic: In year three another Xianbei chieftain was killed, with more than a thousand heads taken.

units.zh: 天福元年十一月己亥，帝御北京崇元殿，降制：「改長興七年為天福元年，大赦天下。
units.literal: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of the first year of Tianfu, the Emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and issued an edict: "Let the seventh year of Changxing be changed to the first year of Tianfu, and grant a general amnesty throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of Tianfu 1, the emperor entered the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and promulgated an edict: "The seventh year of Changxing is hereby renamed Tianfu 1, and a general amnesty is proclaimed for all under Heaven.

units.zh: 十一月九日昧爽已前，應在京及諸州諸色罪犯，及曾授偽命職掌官吏，並見禁囚徒，已結正未結正，已發覺未發覺，罪無輕重，常赦不原者，咸赦除之。
units.literal: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, all offenders of every category in the capital and the various prefectures, officials who had once received appointments from the false regime, and prisoners currently held in custody—whether their cases had been concluded or not, whether discovered or not, regardless of the severity of the offense, and even those normally excluded from routine amnesties—were all pardoned and released.
units.idiomatic: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, every class of offender in the capital and in the provinces, every official who had once held office under the usurper regime, and every prisoner still in custody—case closed or pending, offense known or not, grave or slight, including crimes ordinarily beyond the reach of amnesty—was pardoned and set free.

units.zh: 應明宗朝所行敕命法制，仰所在遵行，不得改易。
units.literal: As for the edicts and regulations promulgated in the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, [authorities] in each locality are to follow them and may not alter them.
units.idiomatic: The edicts and statutes issued in the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong are to be observed everywhere as written, without change.

units.zh: 太常卿梁文矩奏定四廟謚號、廟號、陵號，太常少卿裴垣奏定四廟皇后追尊謚號，從之。
units.literal: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju memorialized on fixing the posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan memorialized on fixing the posthumous honorific titles for the empresses of the four temples; the court approved.
units.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju proposed posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan proposed posthumous titles for the empresses honored there; both were approved.

units.zh: 戊寅，以中書舍人、權知貢舉王延為御史中丞，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎、知制誥崔棁為兵部侍郎充承旨，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎程遜為檢校禮部尚書、太常卿，以檢校吏部尚書、太常卿梁文矩為吏部尚書，以御史中丞張昭遠為戶部侍郎，以吏部尚書盧文紀為太子少傅。
units.literal: On the wuyin day, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, was made Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and drafter of edicts, was made Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin Academician, chief drafter, and Vice Minister of War, was made Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju, Acting Minister of Personnel and Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Lu Wenji, Minister of Personnel, was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
units.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, became Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and rescript drafter, became Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin chief drafter and Vice Minister of War, became Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju became Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan became Vice Minister of Revenue; and Lu Wenji became Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 己卯，詔太社內先收掌唐朝罪人首級等，宜令骨肉或先舊僚屬收葬，其喪葬儀註不得過制。
units.literal: On the jimao day, an edict stated that the severed heads of Tang dynasty convicts previously held at the Altar of Earth should be released to their kin or former colleagues for burial, and that funeral rites must not exceed proper form.
units.idiomatic: On jimao an edict ordered that severed heads of Tang convicts kept at the Altar of Earth be released to kin or former colleagues for burial, with funeral observances kept within proper bounds.
